A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, method, central theory, and benchmarks. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, equations, and figures support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original neural-network and elastic-net classification experiments on LSHTC1, DMOZ, and ODP, including accuracy and training-time results.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds WLSTS comparisons, embedding visualizations, and precision/recall results.

M1.justification: LOCOLE names the existing approach: low-coherence label embeddings, squared-error regression, and nearest-neighbor decoding. The neural-network and elastic-net implementations remain unchanged; the revised meta-algorithm clarifies its inputs without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate extreme multiclass classification on LSHTC1, DMOZ, and ODP. The new visualizations and precision/recall analyses examine retained embeddings and datasets; dynamically growing label spaces are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: WLSTS, previously only discussed as related work, becomes an evaluated comparator in v4 Table 3, with LSHTC1 and DMOZ accuracies and an ODP timeout. The existing comparator set is otherwise retained.

E3.justification: Appendix B.6 adds macro/micro precision and recall evaluation on LSHTC1. B.5 introduces t-SNE visualization of 2,048 vectors from each embedding type. Existing dataset splits, neural-network settings, and elastic-net hyperparameters match across versions.

E4.justification: V4 adds targeted analyses of structural differences between embedding types through t-SNE and whether the coherence trend extends to precision and recall. Existing accuracy-versus-coherence and computational comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy means and standard deviations over five randomized repetitions. V4 introduces no new seed disclosure, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Retained accuracy and runtime values match after percentage conversion. V4 adds WLSTS results of 16.52% on LSHTC1 and 13.60% on DMOZ, an ODP timeout, and supplementary findings. ODP's 128-dimensional rows are omitted from Table 3, although corresponding points remain in Figure 1. The new claim that Nelson-509 is best across all datasets conflicts with ODP's retained Nelson-2039 maximum of 22.30%.

T1.justification: Theorem 4 and its main derivation remain. V4 adds a deterministic-label specialization, a formal Fisher-consistency definition, and Nelson's construction. However, v3's conditional-risk definitions are removed while Appendix A still uses that notation. New Appendix C.2 states a coherence bound of (r-1)/n, conflicting with the (r-1)/sqrt(n) bound retained in the experimental setup.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the coherence-dependent excess-risk bound, lossless embedding under sufficiently low coherence and Massart noise, and effective scalable classification. V3 already disclaimed novelty of the general meta-algorithm; v4's clearer attribution and LOCOLE name do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly notes that Massart's condition is generally unverifiable in practice. It adds guidance on choosing embedding dimensions, discusses capacity limits for growing label spaces, and interprets the deterministic-label case. The conclusion also replaces the claim of linear generalization-error growth with a less specific dependence on output dimension.

D1.justification: V4 adds links to baseline implementations, license information, a direct dataset-access pointer, practical embedding-selection guidance, and an explicit construction formula. It clarifies comparator losses and the 50-hour stopping rule. Existing architecture, optimizer, hardware, and solver details are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds positioning against simplex-encoding consistency results, further consistency references, dataset citations, and explanations for excluding certain comparisons. It recategorizes SLICE as a one-vs-all method and replaces Zhai and Wang with Reeve and Kabán for the generalization discussion. The broader literature framing remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and learning-algorithm exposition are substantially rewritten. Matrix coherence is integrated into the method section, the main-text proof sketch is removed, Proposition 2's proof moves to the appendix, and dedicated limitations and extended-discussion sections reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: V3's three accuracy tables become one side-by-side comparison, and three coherence plots are redrawn as one multi-panel figure. The runtime table is reorganized, a notation table and two supplementary figures are added, and the journal layout substantially changes placement and spacing.

improvement.justification: V4 improves organization, adds a relevant comparator and supplementary analyses, and documents practical limitations and code assets. However, it removes definitions still needed in Appendix A, introduces conflicting Nelson coherence bounds, and misidentifies the best ODP embedding dimension in its results discussion. These benefits and reliability problems coexist without a clear net quality improvement or deterioration.
